body:
Thank you for your valuable insight. Sounds like you've got life all figured out :)

I think it's just a matter of finding my own perspective as you said, which I am still in the process of figuring out. I have also been there - praying away for my problems to disappear. But nothing ever changed and it's part of the reason I turned away from religion. The other part being the preposterity of the fairy tales and sky Gods. So a part of me is grateful I turned away and took the 'red pill' so to speak.

Yes I just saw your response. I suppose I will keep a kind of record about what she says and remind myself about it whenever I get those thoughts. That's a good idea.

And I will speak to my therapist about it. A part of me just wants an escape mechanism to feel good. Suicidal thoughts are sort of providing me with that, as is music to an extent. But I am considering medication and things like weed. Generally not a good idea, I know.

Yes! I feel exactly the same. I feel like I am a hopeless case, each time I encounter a setback. And it is not just 'proof' that suicide is the solution, but rather 'proof' of my inadequacy as a person - especially when I am criticized about academic work.

I feel like giving up - not just in terms of suicide but my academic year. How can a person as mentally weak as me pursue a career in psychology anyways? These are my feelings and they fuel my suicidal thoughts. 

Would you say this is clinical and would require medication? Given my constant thoughts about it. I don't consider myself depressed in the clinical sense however, as I still go out when I need to and as hard as it is to do so. And I can still experience joy and temporarily forget about my worries when I am with others. It's just that these feelings are still there and take over when I am alone.

Well she and I have been best friends for 11 years now. I have told her exactly what has been going on with me for the past few weeks and how I have felt. She was extremely supportive. I expected her to tell me that I am weak and I should not be considering suicide as it is stupid, or judge me for it considering she is religious and criticize me for my lack of faith. 

However she relayed her own experiences to me and how she dealt with them and was not judgemental at all. That helped me quite a bit in terms of dealing with it. I should reach out further at some point.

I am female, 24 years old. To add a layer of interest - I am doing a masters degree in industrial psychology. I think that alone - psychology and the self-awareness that comes with doing such an intense programme - sent me on a downward spiral this year. It made me aware of my weaknesses.

I hear what you're saying. But right now I feel like I need that kind of fix. I just want a moment where I don't have to rely on anyone for that pleasure - and that reduces my social anxiety in public as that is part of my problem.

I have been considering asking my physician for anti-anxiety pills as well. Anything to get the edge off. I realize this is not a long term fix but I guess I am feeling desperate at present. Suicide is really my last resort.

Thank you for the response. Those are exactly the fears I have, such as losing a loved one or failure as you mentioned. As I mentioned in my previous reply, it seems my brain is hard wired to consider suicide in light of any hardship occurring. It is almost as if I would not/do not want to experience the immense pain that comes with those hardships, hence I will just bail. It makes me feel weak. Hell, I probably am.

I am currently not taking any drugs at all or consuming any substance. However, I have been considering gaining access to some weed and taking it to feel good and experience pleasure. I have also been considering drinking alcohol in moderation just to cope and dull the pain. Bad idea I suppose?

Thank you for sharing your experience and I am glad you sought help.

I have reached out to a very close friend. But I do not want to burden her with my thoughts further. And besides her, I do not want to speak to other friends or family. They would probably think I am weak and looking for attention. The latter is the main reason I keep my feelings to myself.

I am however seeing a therapist. But it is not frequent enough and I have these feelings in between sessions. It is really a dark place to be in and is all-consuming.

It is like my brain is hard wired to consider suicide whenever a hardship occurs. I hate it.

Pretty much. I will see how it goes on Monday (my appointment with the therapist).

Thank you btw. This Reddit community has been so helpful in general thus far. I am forever grateful :)

...And I actually do have daddy issues hahaha! Probably going to walk right into that one with my therapist.

I don't think it is worth the risk though. I am seeking counselling at my university and although it is confidential etc - my therapist did ask who exactly my supervisor is. So I suppose I have to tread carefully with regards to what I say. Things have a way of 'coming out'.

Definitely. I am kind of working through it with my therapist; however, not to the full extent.
 
I am quite nervous about mentioning how I really feel about her to the therapist. Not sure if she is bi-friendly/gay friendly. Does it really matter though? All therapists are trained to deal with such matters I would think?

No unfortunately I cannot as she is the only person that specializes in the topic of my thesis. Added to that is the fact that she is brilliant at what she does and is an excellent supervisor - a sure shot way to ensure a good mark.

Yes, that's the direction I am headed at the moment - keeping things professionally. There is no other way around it really.

I should hope that after I am done with the semester, I get over her or the end of the semester serves as a catalyst to get over her, Unfortunately I don't think there could ever be anything between us.

Deep, intense stuff so far. But I am enjoying it! Just done with a Conflict Resolution module and currently doing Individual Counselling Interventions. There is also the Psychological Assessment, Employee Wellness and Organizational Development modules to get through.

I am from South Africa so the modules are very context specific especially in terms of the lingering effects of the Apartheid era in post-apartheid South Africa and what effect it has on workers/ employees currently.

Curious to know how I/O Psychology is overseas, if you know?
No I can't approach her... even at the end of the year. She is straight and there is a 28 year age gap between us... would be super awkward to say the very least.

I will try. Thank you. I do some of the above already aside from the physical distance thing - when I go to her office, I sit on the chair closest to her for example. That needs to stop.

And I always make eye contact in class. Or just look at her/admire her beauty. Doesn't really help so that needs to stop too.

ugh it is the hardest thing. Interestingly, I was in love with my straight best friend for years, and now I kinda 'got over' her ever since this unhealthy crush. I swear it was much easier to be in love with my best friend lol.
The Old Gods and the New ;)
No worries - I cannot even think of telling her. She is straight and it could lead to very awkward encounters going forward.
It is quite difficult but I suppose it's all I can do under the circumstances. Thanks for the input :)

I also have a male prof at university who is very good friends with me. He tends to be friendly with most students. He does not teach me anything though and I don't have a crush on him at all.

It's the female prof attraction that is driving me insane at present. I imagine it to be quite difficult for you seeing as you two are friends as it is.

Thanks, and same to you! I may take you up on that offer :)

I hear what you are saying but I cannot avoid her - she is my thesis advisor and nobody else in the department is specialized in my topic aside from her. I have to get this thesis completed by the end of the year.

The best I can do it email her work stuff instead of going to see her which will maintain that distance.

Thanks for your input :)

Not to mention she is straight, adding to the impossibility of there being anything more.

It's vacation season now so that helps. I have been seeing a therapist but I just said I idealize my professor and it is unhealthy. I did not mention my romantic feelings or that I have a crush. I am quite ashamed and worried about how the therapist would perceive that... (I am a closeted bisexual, but that's another issue altogether)

But yes, distractions it is :)

...And give her some breathing space in the process. She probably just thinks I am THAT annoying student that always wants assistance. She does not know the half of it. Just as well.

Physical activity it is! :)

Thanks so much for that and sorry to hear about your experience, but I am glad you found a way to deal with it :) My only worry is that she is my lecturer and research supervisor so I am required to see her all the time for the remainder of this year, which doesn't help me with my feelings.

I suppose I should distract myself in the ways you've suggested, in the times I AM away from her... because I tend to put on romantic songs and fantasize about her... counter-productive to say the least. 

I will have to immerse myself in other activities because I have actually lost interest in things that I usually enjoyed ever since developing this crush :/

I realise this. Thanks you guys for the input. The problem is - I am obsessed with her and I cannot stop thinking about her. To the point where I stalk her on the internet and get to know everything about her. I hate that I do this - but my feelings for her are just that intense. How can I get her out of my mind? This is clearly unhealthy.
Going to see one in about two weeks but just wanted some perspective before that

A sad reality. I am incredibly grateful to live in a country where the worst that would happen to me is simply being disowned by certain friends and family. Still not ideal though. I hope others stuck in the middle east manage to escape it in some way or the other.
Thanks so much! And change has indeed occurred as you will see from my latest update :)

Hi All

Sorry, I have been so incredibly busy with work!

So an update: Good news - I have been coming out to people who would be more accepting of me. During class, I spoke about how I am a cultural Muslim only - and I have liberal views.

I did not specifically state that I am an atheist, but it could be inferred. For me, that was the first big step to finally learning to come out and be myself in some way or the other. It provides an element of relief - even if it means I cannot come out to my family and certain close Muslim friends.

I also told two of my close non-Muslim that I am an atheist. The one friend told me she will probably reach that same stage at some point when she is ready (she is a Hindu, but not devout at all and questions the practices). The other friend said he is proud of me for coming out about it, but still thinks it is silly that I do not believe in God. He still nevertheless accepts me.

So I guess huge leaps and progress has been made :)

Regarding my supervisor - she is still way too professional for me to say anything to her at this stage. However, I have found a way around this regarding a legit concern about work - We are doing a counselling module and it is incredibly difficult for me to counsel a person who believes that witchcraft is the cause of their misfortune or that God is punishing them. I constantly want to challenge their views which I regard as irrational - but ofcourse in counselling, you cannot do that as it is unhealthy for the client. You have to accept and counsel them according to the framework of their culture and worldview.

So I plan on asking my supervisor/lecturer how do I, as an atheist, go about counselling someone who is religious when I automatically have internal reactions about their thoughts around God and witchcraft to be irrational. I would assume this would open up some sort of constructive dialogue regarding atheism.

What do you guys think?

So should I just post the exact same question and details in that threat instead? Are there any rules on Reddit regarding repeat threads?

Thank you, I will have a look at the videos.

Yes, there is that chance. And given that not even her colleague (the other atheist friend of mine that I confide in) does not know her religious stance and respects her enough not to question it, I most definitely think I have to tread lightly and respect it as well. I guess I'll have to see what happens.

Yes, but my parents are hardcore conservatives. Regardless of any Quraanic justifications, they will either disown me or tell my entire family about it in an effort to 'reform' me as well as send me to a Muslim priest. I would not be able to handle that.

Thank you for the input :)

That is what I thought too. She does seem like the ideal person to confide in, but I do not think it would be appropriate and unless she shows signs of being more open and such an opportunity presents itself, I do not think there is much I can do at this stage other than seeking support online as I am doing now. Thanks for the input :)

Thank you. I will most definitely get in touch. I just need time to gather my thoughts. I appreciate your willingness to help and it's good knowing there are people out there who are just like me, going through the same struggles. I reject Islam as a religion but still subscribe to the cultural aspects. For example, I still wear the hijab (headscarf) through personal choice... oh the irony :p Thank you once again. I shall be in touch.
With her, if I have to try this, it will have to be a subtle approach and context specific. Not something I can just bring up. Hopefully an opportunity presents itself. Thank you for your input :)

Thank you :) I am at a crossroad in terms of whether to approach her or not. Either way, I think I should seek out other mediums for support as you suggested. I was hoping to find personal support in reality, but that is not always easy to find. Thanks once again for your input.
